tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Get the owner's professional profile summary, plus nextSteps — concrete ways to continue (contact channels, GitHub, MCP connect). Use it as the first tool in an interview.

tools.name: get_projects
tools.description: Get portfolio projects with stack, highlights, and decision logs. Optional filter by stack tag.

tools.name: search_projects
tools.description: Free-text search across portfolio projects — name, tagline, description, stack and decision-log rationale. Returns matched projects with a score and the fields that matched. Use when a fixed stack-tag filter is too narrow (e.g. 'RAG', 'latency', 'Zed'). Read-only, closed world.

tools.name: get_engineering_principles
tools.description: Get engineering principles with real examples and A/B-style counterfactuals.

tools.name: get_articles
tools.description: Get recent Dev.to articles with reading time, tags and links.

tools.name: get_commit_history
tools.description: Get recent commit history across the owner's public repos (hourly snapshot). Use it to answer 'what has he been building lately' or 'show the hardest bugs he has fixed'.

tools.name: get_antipatterns
tools.description: Get the owner's antipattern museum — real engineering mistakes with why they were bad, how they were fixed, and the lesson. Read-only, closed world.

tools.name: analyze_stack
tools.description: Compare the owner's stack against a job's required skills. Returns per-skill match with evidence and coverage.

tools.name: simulate_architecture
tools.description: Simulate how a project's architecture behaves under a scenario (load spike, node loss, cache cold, LLM saturation). Returns latency percentiles per load and bottleneck analysis.

tools.name: get_experiments
tools.description: Get the owner's engineering experiments — hypothesis, command, raw result and verdict (confirmed/refuted/partial) for each. Use it to answer 'what did you measure' or 'show me an experiment you ran'. Includes negative results (approaches that failed). Read-only, closed world.

tools.name: get_diary
tools.description: Get the owner's engineering diary — incidents, root causes, fixes and guards, each tagged with a pattern (NEW vs recurring). Use it to answer 'what broke and how did you fix it' or 'show your hardest debugging session'. Read-only, closed world.

tools.name: get_known_issues
tools.description: Get the owner's known-issues board — open debt with status, temperature (stable/watching) and deadlines. Use it to answer 'what's still broken' or 'what are you working on'. Read-only, closed world.

tools.name: get_issue_detail
tools.description: Get the full detail of a single known issue by its ID (e.g. 'KI-109'). Drills into one open problem: status, temperature, owner, linked source and the raw problem statement. Returns a clear not-found with the available IDs if the ID does not match. Read-only, closed world.

tools.name: verify_claim
tools.description: Ground a claim about the owner against the portfolio's data (profile, projects, principles, timeline, antipatterns, experiments, diary, known issues). findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_known_issues, get_issue_detail, verify_claim, verify_article · Private data: get_profile, verify_claim, verify_repo · Public sink: verify_package.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_known_issues, get_issue_detail, verify_claim, verify_article · Private data: get_profile, verify_claim, verify_repo · Public sink: verify_package

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
